capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- For the Möbius-action identity, represent \(g\) by
  \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\). The action is
  \((az+b)/(cz+d)\); replacing \(g\) by \(-g\) negates both numerator and denominator, so the quotient—and hence the induced point of `UpperHalfPlane`—is unchanged.

- For zeta, use the absolutely convergent Dirichlet-series representation for \(x>1\):
  \[
  \zeta(x)=\sum_{n\ge1} n^{-x}.
  \]
  Every term is real and nonnegative, while the \(n=1\) term is \(1\), so the sum is a strictly positive real number. Organize this by first showing `riemannZeta (Complex.ofReal x)` has zero imaginary part, then proving its real part is positive, and finally translating those facts into Mathlib’s partial-order statement \(0<\zeta(x)\) in `Complex`. Existing L-series positivity lemmas should package most of this second step.
